## Presentation Title
**Origin of the Bean: Ethiopia in Every Cup**  
*An editorial journey through highland farms, ancient ritual, and the birthplace of coffee*

## Style Direction
- Cinematic premium documentary meets luxury editorial travel magazine
- Warm, tactile, human, atmospheric — like a Netflix food-culture film with Monocle/Kinfolk polish
- Should feel slow, sensory, reverent: misty mountains, sun-dried cherries, incense smoke, clay jebena, farmers’ hands
- Avoid generic café aesthetics, corporate coffee slides, clip-art beans, overused latte imagery, tourist-board clichés
- Every slide should feel like a curated magazine spread captured in golden-hour 35mm film

## Core Artistic Direction
- Full-bleed cinematic photography: Ethiopian highlands, coffee forests, red cherries, woven baskets, drying beds, intimate portraits, buna ceremony details
- Premium editorial typography: elegant serif hero titles, restrained sans-serif body text, small uppercase captions with generous tracking
- Earth-rich palette: roasted brown, parchment cream, cherry red, forest green, clay terracotta, golden sunrise, soft smoke gray
- Layout mood: asymmetrical magazine grids, bold negative space, oversized pull quotes, thin rule lines, refined caption systems
- Textures/effects: subtle film grain, warm paper fibers, soft vignettes, dust motes, incense haze, sun flare, tactile coffee-stain accents used sparingly
- Visual rhythm: alternate grand landscape hero slides with intimate macro-detail spreads and quiet cultural portrait moments
- Diagram style: hand-drawn origin maps, elegant process timelines, refined tasting-note wheels, minimal editorial infographics
- Animation energy: slow Ken Burns image drift, gentle crossfades, text rising softly like steam, map lines drawing by hand, warm light leaks between sections

## Color Palette

**Highland Espresso** `#24160F` — primary deep background, title overlays, cinematic shadows.  
**Roasted Umber** `#4A2C1A` — rich editorial panels, section dividers, coffee-bean details.  
**Bunna Clay** `#8C4A2F` — warm cultural accent, callouts, ceremony-inspired highlights.  
**Sun-Dried Cherry** `#B43A2E` — premium red accent for coffee cherries, key data points, emphasis.  
**Jebena Black** `#0E0B08` — luxury contrast, footer bars, dramatic typography moments.  
**Golden Crema** `#C9944A` — metallic highlight, icons, thin rules, premium glow effects.  
**Highland Mist** `#EFE6DA` — warm off-white backgrounds, editorial whitespace, text cards.  
**Parchment Cream** `#F7F0E6` — soft reading surfaces, captions, map backgrounds.  
**Yirgacheffe Green** `#586B45` — landscape accents, origin maps, botanical notes.  
**Blue Nile Dusk** `#2F4656` — cool cinematic balance, map shadows, evening documentary scenes.  

## Typography

**Hero Display: Canela Deck** — 72–120pt, regular/italic, cinematic cover titles and poetic statements.  
**Editorial Serif: Editorial New** — 44–72pt, medium, section openers and premium magazine headlines.  
**Body Narrative: Söhne** — 18–26pt, regular, documentary storytelling paragraphs and slide copy.  
**Caption Mono: Söhne Mono** — 11–14pt, medium/all caps, photo credits, region labels, tasting notes.  
**Map / Annotation Hand: Reenie Beanie** — 18–32pt, regular, handwritten map notes, origin markers, cultural details.  

| Hierarchy | Size |
|---|---:|
| Hero | 96–120pt |
| Section | 56–72pt |
| Body | 18–26pt |
| Caption | 11–14pt |

## Layout System
- 12-column editorial grid with generous negative space; 96px outer margins, 32px gutters, strict baseline alignment.
- Use cinematic full-bleed hero photography for emotional slides; keep text anchored in lower-left or upper-right safe zones.
- Alternate between immersive documentary spreads, luxury magazine feature layouts, map-led origin pages, and premium process-diagram compositions.
- Image rules: one dominant visual per slide; secondary images only as refined editorial insets, contact-sheet strips, or framed archival details.
- Typography hierarchy: oversized serif headlines, small all-caps mono captions, elegant body copy blocks limited to short poetic paragraphs.
- Composition rhythm: wide landscape establishing shots, intimate macro close-ups, human portrait spreads, and minimal data/story diagrams.

## Animation Style
- Transitions: slow cinematic cross-dissolves, gentle film cuts, and soft parallax pushes; avoid flashy PowerPoint-style wipes.
- Entrance effects: text fades upward subtly with 200–350ms stagger; captions appear last like magazine annotations.
- Motion pacing: slow, premium, documentary-like; 900–1200ms transitions with ease-in-out cubic easing.
- Photography motion: restrained Ken Burns zooms, horizontal drift across highland landscapes, and soft focus pulls on coffee cherries or hands.
- Diagram motion: maps draw in like ink on parchment; origin markers pulse softly; processing steps reveal sequentially like documentary chapter beats.
- Atmosphere effects: floating dust, warm steam, sunlight leaks, subtle grain shimmer, and slow smoke movement around jebena ceremony scenes.

## Visual Requirements
- Photography style: cinematic Ethiopian highlands, golden-hour farms, intimate farmer portraits, macro cherries, drying beds, roasting, jebena ceremony.
- Color grade: roasted browns, clay reds, deep greens, warm cream, black coffee shadows, amber highlights; premium matte documentary finish.
- Illustration type: hand-drawn cartographic accents, botanical coffee-plant sketches, small cultural motifs, elegant line icons.
- Diagram aesthetic: editorial infographics with thin rules, serif labels, muted earth tones, minimal callouts, and atlas-inspired annotations.
- Texture/overlays: subtle 35mm film grain, warm paper fiber, faint dust, soft vignette, gentle light leaks, parchment map layers.
- Avoid generic stock visuals; every image should feel location-specific, tactile, human, and worthy of a luxury travel magazine feature.

## Slide-by-Slide Structure

**Slide 1 — Where the First Bean Woke**
- Mood: Mythic, dawn-lit, reverent — the opening frame of a luxury documentary about origin, memory, and land.
- Layout: Full-bleed cinematic hero image with title anchored low-left; a small editorial location caption sits top-right like a magazine folio: “ETHIOPIA / ORIGIN OF COFFEE.”
- Visual: Mist rolling over Ethiopian highlands at sunrise, silhouettes of coffee trees in the foreground, distant mountains softened by golden haze; subtle film grain and lens bloom.
- FX: Slow Ken Burns push into the valley; title fades in like ink on paper; faint floating dust particles caught in morning light.
- Color: Deep coffee brown, highland green, warm amber sunrise, soft ivory mist, muted black shadows.
- Type: Large elegant serif title, cinematic and spacious; small uppercase mono captioning for location and date; minimal text, premium editorial restraint.

**Slide 2 — The Legend of Kaldi**
- Mood: Storybook documentary, ancient yet intimate — folklore treated with cinematic seriousness and poetic warmth.
- Layout: Split editorial composition: left 60% painterly cinematic scene, right 40% parchment-toned text column with oversized pull quote.
- Visual: A young Ethiopian goat herder on a hillside watching energetic goats near red coffee cherries; illustrated-photo hybrid style, like a museum-quality documentary reenactment.
- FX: Gentle parallax between hillside, goats, and sky; red cherries glow subtly; handwritten line animation traces the path from goat to berry to discovery.
- Color: Clay red, roasted brown, parchment cream, acacia gold, dusk olive, berry crimson accents.
- Type: Refined serif headline; italic pull quote: “A restless goat, a curious boy, and a fruit that changed the world.” Body text in clean editorial sans with generous line spacing.

**Slide 3 — Ethiopia’s Living Coffee Map**
- Mood: Exploratory, premium cartographic, grounded in terroir — like opening a rare atlas of flavor.
- Layout: Full-screen textured map of Ethiopia centered on the slide; region labels arranged as elegant floating callout cards around the map.
- Visual: Hand-drawn luxury map marking Sidama, Yirgacheffe, Harrar, Guji, Limu, Jimma, and Lekempti; each region paired with one sensory note: jasmine, citrus, blueberry, honey, cocoa, spice.
- FX: Map lines draw on as if by fountain pen; coffee-region dots pulse softly; callout cards appear one by one with a subtle paper-slide motion.
- Color: Warm ivory paper, ink brown outlines, deep green terrain washes, cherry-red pins, gold foil micro-accents.
- Type: Sophisticated serif for region names; small uppercase mono for tasting notes; title placed top-left like a premium travel magazine spread.

### ACT II

**Slide 4 — The Highlands Where Coffee Breathes**
- Mood: Misty, sacred, cinematic; an early-morning documentary frame where altitude feels alive and every hillside seems to whisper origin.
- Layout: Full-bleed panoramic image with a thin editorial text column floating on the left; small coordinate-style location tag in the upper-right; subtle contour-line overlay across the landscape.
- Visual: Ethiopian highland coffee forests at dawn, layered mountains, silver fog, wild coffee trees, farmers walking as tiny silhouettes through the mist; premium National Geographic-style photography with soft film grain.
- FX: Slow Ken Burns drift forward through the fog; animated contour lines gently drawing across the terrain; faint light leak from the rising sun; text fades in like a documentary title card.
- Color: Highland mist gray, deep forest green, warm sunrise gold, roasted brown shadows, creamy parchment highlights.
- Type: Large elegant serif title in lower-left; small mono-labels for altitude, region, and climate; body copy set like an editorial field note.

**Slide 5 — Red Cherries, Human Hands**
- Mood: Intimate, tactile, reverent; the quiet dignity of hand-harvesting captured like luxury editorial portraiture.
- Layout: Split editorial composition: left side full-height macro photograph of red coffee cherries in a farmer’s hands; right side warm off-white paper field with three refined process notes.
- Visual: Close-up of weathered hands holding ripe crimson cherries, woven basket texture, soft natural light, shallow depth of field; tiny illustrated arrows identifying cherry skin, pulp, mucilage, seed.
- FX: Subtle parallax between hands and background; animated line annotations gently appear one by one; fine dust particles floating in sunlight; soft shutter-click transition.
- Color: Sun-dried cherry red, clay earth, skin-warm browns, ivory paper, muted leaf green accents.
- Type: Oversized serif headline stacked vertically; annotation labels in delicate mono type; process notes in crisp editorial sans with generous line spacing.

**Slide 6 — Washed by Mountain Water**
- Mood: Clean, rhythmic, luminous; a cinematic sequence of transformation from fruit to green bean.
- Layout: Horizontal filmstrip across the center showing four stages: sorting, pulping, washing, drying; above it a poetic headline; below it a minimal timeline with icons and micro-captions.
- Visual: Documentary stills of washing stations, wooden drying beds, glistening beans, mountain streams, workers sorting coffee by hand; elegant technical overlays showing water flow and fermentation time.
- FX: Waterline animation flows softly across the slide; each process frame reveals with a gentle cinematic wipe; tiny bubbles and light reflections shimmer over the washing image.
- Color: Clear mountain blue, parchment cream, washed bean beige, wet wood brown, restrained green accents.
- Type: Refined serif headline centered with airy spacing; timeline labels in all-caps mono; micro-explanations in clean magazine-style body type.

**Slide 7 — Sun-Drying on Raised Beds**
- Mood: Golden, patient, meditative; the slow craft of drying shown as a sunlit ritual of precision and time.
- Layout: Full-bleed overhead photograph of raised drying beds forming elegant diagonal patterns; translucent editorial cards placed along the diagonals showing time, moisture, and care points.
- Visual: Coffee beans spread across mesh beds under Ethiopian sun, workers turning beans by hand, long shadows, woven textures, amber afternoon light; include a refined moisture curve diagram subtly embedded in the lower-right.
- FX: Warm sunlight slowly sweeps across the beans; animated moisture curve draws from 60% to 11%; soft grain texture; gentle ambient movement like heat shimmer.
- Color: Golden hour amber, raw coffee beige, roasted umber, linen white, soft terracotta, deep shadow brown.
- Type: Cinematic serif title placed top-left; data cards in minimalist sans; mono numerals for drying duration and moisture percentage, styled like a premium agricultural journal.

**Slide 8 — The Ceremony of Smoke & Silence**
- Mood: Sacred, intimate, slow-burning documentary elegance — a quiet living-room ritual where coffee becomes hospitality, memory, and blessing.
- Layout: Full-bleed cinematic interior photo with a low table ceremony scene; negative space preserved in the upper-left for title; small editorial caption strip along the bottom edge like a luxury magazine feature.
- Visual: Ethiopian coffee ceremony with jebena, incense smoke, grass floor covering, small porcelain cups, roasted beans in a woven tray; shot in warm natural window light, shallow depth of field, tactile and human.
- FX: Slow smoke drift animation, gentle candlelike light flicker, subtle Ken Burns push toward the jebena; captions fade in one by one like documentary subtitles.
- Color: Deep coffee brown, incense charcoal, warm clay, cream porcelain, muted green grass accents, soft amber highlights.
- Type: Large cinematic serif title in warm cream, bottom-left; small mono-style cultural notes in uppercase with generous tracking; one elegant pull quote: “Coffee is never rushed here.”

**Slide 9 — Three Cups, Three Invitations**
- Mood: Poetic, hospitable, ceremonial — the emotional rhythm of abol, tona, and baraka unfolding like chapters in a quiet film.
- Layout: Triptych editorial composition: three vertical image panels across the slide, each representing one cup of the ceremony; thin golden divider lines; minimal explanatory text beneath each panel.
- Visual: Cup 1 close-up being poured, Cup 2 hands receiving coffee, Cup 3 empty cups resting beside incense and popcorn; cinematic macro photography with visible steam and hand texture.
- FX: Sequential reveal from left to right; steam rises softly from each cup; tiny glowing particles drift around the third cup to suggest blessing and closure.
- Color: Espresso black, roasted sienna, antique gold, ivory paper, soft smoke gray.
- Type: Oversized serif numerals “I / II / III” behind each panel at 15% opacity; cup names in refined serif; descriptions in clean editorial sans, restrained and spacious.

**Slide 10 — Flavor Written by Altitude**
- Mood: Intelligent, sensory, premium — a refined tasting-room slide where geography becomes aroma, acidity, and texture.
- Layout: Split-screen: left side an elegant altitude diagram rising through Ethiopian highlands; right side a premium tasting-note card with flavor clusters arranged like a wine menu.
- Visual: Minimal illustrated mountain profile with coffee regions marked by elevation bands; delicate icons for jasmine, bergamot, blueberry, honey, cacao, tea-like finish; background resembles textured tasting paper.
- FX: Altitude line draws upward with a fine ink animation; flavor notes appear as soft stamped labels; subtle shimmer on region markers.
- Color: Highland cream background, Yirgacheffe green, sun-dried cherry red, golden honey, dark roast brown, misty blue-gray.
- Type: Serif headline top-right; tasting notes in elegant stacked hierarchy; mono captions for elevation ranges and region names, styled like archival field notes.

**Slide 11 — The Hands Behind the Harvest**
- Mood: Human, dignified, cinematic — a portrait of labor, pride, and generational knowledge without sentimentality or cliché.
- Layout: Premium editorial portrait grid: one large hero portrait on the left, three smaller documentary detail frames on the right; quote block anchored in the lower-right margin.
- Visual: Ethiopian coffee farmer holding freshly picked cherries; supporting frames show sorting hands, woven baskets, drying beds, and sunlit beans; authentic documentary photography with natural skin tones and soft grain.
- FX: Gentle parallax between portrait and detail images; handwritten region annotation draws in near the basket; quote fades in last with a soft paper-texture reveal.
- Color: Earth brown, cherry red, linen beige, leaf green, sun-warmed ochre, soft black typography.
- Type: Elegant serif title over the portrait edge; farmer quote in large italic editorial style; small uppercase metadata: region, altitude, harvest season, process.

**Slide 12 — The Economics of a Single Cup**
- Mood: Premium documentary realism; quiet, intelligent, human-centered, revealing the hidden value chain behind Ethiopian coffee.
- Layout: Split editorial composition: left side full-height portrait of a farmer weighing freshly harvested cherries; right side layered transparent value-chain diagram flowing vertically from **farm → washing station → exporter → roaster → café → consumer**. Add small KPI-style price markers, but keep them elegant and minimal.
- Visual: Cinematic natural-light photography, tactile details of hands, burlap sacks, metal scales, handwritten receipts, coffee cherries in woven baskets. Overlay refined infographic lines like thin gold thread tracing the journey.
- FX: Slow camera push into the farmer’s hands; value-chain lines animate one segment at a time; numbers softly count up; subtle paper-grain texture over the whole slide.
- Color: Deep espresso brown, parchment cream, muted gold, washed olive green, cherry red accents used sparingly for key value points.
- Type: Large editorial serif title upper-left on the diagram side; small mono captions for prices and locations; one quiet pull quote near the bottom: *“Behind every export figure is a harvest, a family, a season.”*

**Slide 13 — Women at the Heart of the Harvest**
- Mood: Intimate, dignified, luminous; a premium editorial tribute to the women who sort, wash, dry, roast, and serve coffee across Ethiopia.
- Layout: Magazine photo essay grid: one large cinematic hero portrait occupying 60% of the slide, with three smaller detail images stacked beside it — hands sorting beans, a woman roasting over fire, coffee poured from a jebena. Use generous margins and elegant captioning.
- Visual: Documentary portraiture with warm window light, shallow depth of field, authentic clothing textures, woven stools, clay cups, smoke, sunlight through fabric. No posed corporate imagery — everything should feel observed, respectful, real.
- FX: Soft dissolve between portrait layers; gentle smoke animation rising from the roasting pan; micro-glow on embers; captions appear like printed editorial annotations.
- Color: Warm clay, charcoal black, cream linen, ember orange, deep coffee brown, subtle red cherry highlights.
- Type: Serif headline placed vertically along the left margin; captions in refined small caps; one handwritten-style annotation circling the sorting tray: *“selection begins by eye, by hand, by memory.”*

**Slide 14 — Ethiopia in the Global Cup**
- Mood: Expansive, worldly, cinematic; Ethiopia as both origin and influence, connecting highland farms to cafés across the planet.
- Layout: Dark premium map spread: Ethiopia glows at the center-left, with luminous trade routes arcing toward Tokyo, London, New York, Seoul, Dubai, Melbourne, and Copenhagen. On the right, floating editorial cards show cup profiles and café moments from around the world.
- Visual: Elegant atlas-style world map with topographic texture, glowing origin pin over Ethiopia, animated golden route lines, small cinematic café vignettes in rounded rectangular frames. Include subtle coffee-stain rings as texture, not decoration.
- FX: Routes draw outward slowly like constellations; destination cards fade in with parallax; tiny particles travel along the arcs like sparks from a roast drum.
- Color: Midnight espresso, antique gold, soft cream, highland green, muted terracotta, faint blue-gray for oceans.
- Type: Large refined serif title across the top: *“From the Highlands to the World.”* Destination labels in mono type; flavor notes in elegant italic beneath each city card.

**Slide 15 — The Cup Returns to the Mountain**
- Mood: Poetic, cinematic closing; emotional, slow, reverent — a final frame that feels like the end of a premium Netflix documentary.
- Layout: Full-bleed golden-hour landscape of Ethiopian coffee highlands, mist drifting through trees. Centered closing line in large serif typography, with a small ceremonial cup silhouette at the bottom. Minimal layout, maximum atmosphere.
- Visual: Wide panoramic shot of terraced hills, coffee trees, distant village rooftops, soft smoke rising from a home, sunlight breaking through morning fog. Add faint overlay of handwritten Amharic-inspired texture and botanical coffee-plant line art in the corners.
- FX: Slow Ken Burns pullback; mist subtly moves across the valley; sunlight blooms gently; final text fades in after a cinematic pause; tiny dust particles shimmer in the light.
- Color: Golden amber, deep forest green, warm cream, roasted brown, soft mist gray, delicate white glow.
- Type: Large centered editorial serif: *“Every cup begins as a place.”* Small mono subtitle below: *“Ethiopia — origin, ritual, memory.”* Final text should feel printed into the light, not simply placed on top.
